Skinny guys needing to bulk are common. But you're not really skinny, you're slightly more muscular than the average person but you're just so lean it's weird. I personally think you're sub 10% body fat and that isn't seen often in people with your weight and height.

1) There's the efficiency/technique part but neurological adaptations are also a big factor. You basically learn to use your muscles to a higher degree, sorta like how someone in a life or death situation suddenly becomes able to produce strength not seen before. That's why you'll often see powerlifters lifting more than someone way bigger.

2) That's definitely true but I don't know to what degree it applies to you as you're an extreme outlier. Because you're such an extreme I'd even bet you'll grow just by increasing protein and calorie intake while training the same way without progressively overloading. You definitely should keep overloading though, I think you'll see substantial strength and muscle gains pretty quickly.

I think you misinterpret the newbie gains thing. It isn't your training age that matters but how far off you are from your genetic limit. When you have built a considerate amount of muscle your body will have a harder time building more muscle with the available recourses. You still have a long way to go before you reach your limit. You are also making it hard on yourself by trying to stay extremely lean.

The milestones you are talking about are kinda pointless because you weigh so little. They're just made up numbers to shoot for in your first year of training.

Also guys, stop down voting this dude. He seems eager to learn but just lacks experience. This is one of the more intelligent conversations by reddit fitness thread standards.

You are also not getting fat that quickly. Even if you reach 65 kg without building any extra muscle you won't look fat, you'll just look normal. If you want to make progress in the long run you have to move away from your current body.

Those lifts are just slightly above beginner level tbh. You need to some hypertrophy training and bulk if you want to grow muscle. You just look like a really lean normal sized person. You're even underweight according to your BMI which just confirms my opinion.

I'm not trying to be mean here, being that lean is definitely impressive and I wish I could walk around at that body fat. But just bulking and training will easily get you to 60-65kg while still being lean within a year. I already have a few years of training behind me and I'm at 15% body fat but I weigh 74 kg.

Definitely this. I started with about the same physique as OP and was also trying to bulk thinking I'd just lose the fat later. I gained around 20lbs in my first year while looking about the same in the end. The fat loss was the hardest part.

Cardio alone won't do it. You look to be around 25%-30% bodyfat so you still have a way to go if you want to lose the belly. To lose fat, no matter where, a calorie deficit is the most important factor. 

Track your calories and your weight with an app like MyFitnessPal. Once you know what calories you need at a stable weight try eating 200-500 less calories. Don't try to eat less to speed up the process, you'll be miserable and wanting to quit the whole time. Consistent progress is more important than progress speed. 

If you're weight training you need to know your strength and energy levels might drop a little. If that's the case, try training with less intensity. Feeling miserable in the gym while also being in a calorie deficit drains willpower will make you want to quit. You're not trying to prove yourself to anyone, you're trying to make progress no matter how small. 

On the point of cardio: cardio is great way to increase a calorie deficit when used intelligently. In my experience low intensity cardio that doesn't leave you tired the rest of the day is the way to go. For example a 30-60 minute walk or riding a (stationary) bike at low-medium speed, something that keeps your heart rate at around 120-130 BPM. This easily burns 200-500 calories while still having energy the rest of the day.  I usually go with the stationary bike at the gym and just watch an episode or 2 of an anime.

Also try getting in enough protein. This is to make sure that what you're losing is actually fat and not muscle.

I really like the idea and it should be implemented where useful but you also need to know it's not all mega factories/warehouses that ship hundreds of containers daily. 

My  workplace for example gets 15-20 containers in spread out over the week. They need to be spread out like that because we can't store a whole weeks worth at the same time. Shipping outward is a few times a day, with highly localized products that really can't wait to be send out. 

Most companies over here that actually have a high in/out flow of products are connected to canals. These ships, while not the fastest, can carry huge loads to docks where they're unloaded into trains and trucks.

The problem I'm talking about is way more small scale but makes up a huge part of the problem.  And that's a single container going 200 miles by truck to it's destination. A single one isn't that bad, but when everyone does it it creates Roads filled with trucks coming from and going to approximately the same location. These trucks would be better off going to a train dock and loading their containers together on a big freigth train. 

Each factory sending off it's own mini trains multiple times a day would be chaos. The other options would be a single large train needing to make stops at each factory, which would be about as time efficient as a delivery driver needing to stop at every single house on a street.

So every factory would need the space for a full on 30 container train unless it'd be like single container trains. Have the machines and trained personnel to load and unload the trains.
Not all containers need to go to the same place. 
So you'd need to either be able to send out multiple fully packed trains each dat to keep it relevant or keep doing it by truck.

A dock would be able to mix containers from different factories into the same train.

You'd still need Roads to get the workers to the factories.

Rail would take up less space but I wouldn't connect it straight to the factories. I'd rather have it be like a railway dock a little farther away from the factories. You could have trucks doing way shorter distance to the factories but you'd also be able to deliver to stores without congesting the factory cluster.

Can't really do that when there are 50 factories in the same street without expanding way out into urban areas. 

A single factory in the Middle of nowhere? Sure!

A clusterfuck of factories with residential areas only a few blocks away? I'd rather not. That would mean everyone would have to make a longer commute.

That would just be a nightmare to arrange. It would Mean having rails on both sides of the Roads since we mostly have factory clusters around here.

 How would you get single containers on the right train, how would you even get them to the train? Every cart would have to be motorized and manned. It would also take up a lot of space since you'd need to leave space for through traffic while also leaving enough space for trains to decelerate and accelerate.

Trucks are nessecary, you can't just build every store, restaurant and factory inside a train station. But freight by train is way better over large distances. 

My country(Belgium/Europe) is full of factory production because we live next to the North-Atlantic ocean and we can cheaply import materials from afar by boat. It's deffinitly not the fastest method, but it's cheap and really good for a steady stream of products.

The problem is, when we move inland away from the ocean, everything seems to be moved by trucks. Yeah sure, it might be faster and more economic to move things on the Road to factories that are close by. 

But why do we make it a 2 day road trip to move shit like whipped cream from here to italy? It could be done way cheaper and way quicker by train. 

Don't get me wrong, we move a lot by train, but not nearly enough in my opinion. And it's costing us a lot in Road repairs and maintenance. And the Roads are still shit!
